spec.expr:
sum by (region) (
  rate(caddy_http_request_duration_seconds_count{service_name=~"appliance-.*-caddy", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)", code=~"5.."}[5m])
) * 60
or
sum by (region) (
  rate(caddy_http_request_duration_seconds_count{service_name=~"appliance-.*-caddy", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"}[5m])
) * 0

spec.description: One row per appliance region. Each cell is a sparkline over the dashboard time range; the number beside it is the reduction: Status and Reconcile age = last value, CPU / Memory / Requests = mean, Disk and 5xx = max (worst filesystem, worst minute). Status is the host node-exporter scrape (up), so it says the box is reachable and Alloy is pushing. Reconcile age turns red past 15 minutes, which is when the node has stopped reconciling. Status counts how many of the region's two scrapes answered, the host exporter and Caddy: the word is the state now (up = both, partial = one, down = neither) and the grey bars are the same count across the window, full height for both, half for one, a stub for neither. A notch in the bars is an incident, and its position is when. The bar colour is constant and means nothing. Requests and 5xx read no data rather than zero when the Caddy scrape is dark. Click a region to open its tab.
spec.title: Appliance health

spec.description: Both scrapes for this region, split by node. Two boxes in one stage and region share service_name and are told apart by node.
spec.title: Status

spec.description: Share of a core spent in each non-idle mode, averaged across cores. Stacked, so the top of the stack is total CPU busy.
spec.title: CPU

spec.description: Fraction of RAM not available to a new allocation. MemAvailable already discounts reclaimable cache, so this is closer to real pressure than used/total.
spec.title: Memory used

spec.description: Run-queue length. Compare against the box's core count: sustained load5 above that is saturation.
spec.title: Load average

spec.description: Throughput per block device from the diskstats collector.
spec.title: Disk I/O

spec.expr:
1 - node_filesystem_avail_bytes{service_name=~"appliance-.*-host", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)", fstype!~"tmpfs|vfat|squashfs|overlay", mountpoint!~"/boot.*"}
  / node_filesystem_size_bytes{service_name=~"appliance-.*-host", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)", fstype!~"tmpfs|vfat|squashfs|overlay", mountpoint!~"/boot.*"}

spec.description: Used fraction per real filesystem. Not stacked: these are independent ratios and a stacked total of them means nothing.
spec.title: Disk Space Usage

spec.expr:
1 - node_filesystem_files_free{service_name=~"appliance-.*-host", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)", fstype!~"tmpfs|vfat|squashfs|overlay", mountpoint!~"/boot.*"}
  / node_filesystem_files{service_name=~"appliance-.*-host", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)", fstype!~"tmpfs|vfat|squashfs|overlay", mountpoint!~"/boot.*"}

spec.description: Used inodes per filesystem. A volume with free bytes and no free inodes fails writes the same way a full one does.
spec.title: Inode Usage

spec.description: Every public request the appliance served, split by site and HTTP method, stacked so the top of the stack is total traffic. Method is the only operation kind Caddy sees: an S3 PutObject is a PUT to a bucket path, so PUT against the s3. host is the upload path. Read from the duration histogram's count, because caddy_http_requests_total carries neither a code nor a method label.
spec.title: Request rate

spec.description: 5xx split by site, handler and code. A 502 is Caddy failing to reach the upstream; a 500 came from Piri or Ingot itself.
spec.title: Server errors

spec.expr:
sum by (host) (
  rate(caddy_http_request_duration_seconds_sum{service_name=~"appliance-.*-caddy", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"}[5m])
)
/
sum by (host) (
  rate(caddy_http_request_duration_seconds_count{service_name=~"appliance-.*-caddy", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"}[5m])
)

spec.description: Round-trip time to last byte, per site: caddy_http_request_duration_seconds, the whole request. TTFB is the panel beside it. The average is sum/count; p95 reads the histogram buckets.
spec.title: Response time

spec.description: Age of each project's last successful pass, from the deploy stamp the reconcile timer writes through the textfile collector. The timer runs every five minutes, so a reconcile age past the 15-minute threshold line means the node has stopped reconciling. apps and platform move only when that project actually deployed, so they climb between releases and that is normal.
spec.title: Time since last deploy

spec.expr:
sum by (host) (
  rate(caddy_http_request_duration_seconds_count{service_name=~"appliance-.*-caddy", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)", code=~"5.."}[5m])
)
/
sum by (host) (
  rate(caddy_http_request_duration_seconds_count{service_name=~"appliance-.*-caddy", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"}[5m])
)
or
sum by (host) (
  rate(caddy_http_request_duration_seconds_count{service_name=~"appliance-.*-caddy", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"}[5m])
) * 0

spec.description: 5xx responses as a share of everything the site served. The trailing `or ... * 0` holds the line at zero for a site with traffic and no errors; a site with no data at all drops out rather than reading zero. Threshold lines at 1% and 5%.
spec.title: Error rate

spec.description: Bytes in and out through Caddy, which is every public request the region serves. Taken from the histograms' _sum, so the figure is exact and does not depend on the size buckets. The node exporter's network collector is not shipped, so this is the appliance's traffic rather than the host interface's.
spec.title: Ingress / egress

spec.description: Time to first byte, p95, per site and method. caddy_http_response_duration_seconds is Caddy's own "times to first byte in response bodies" histogram, distinct from request_duration_seconds, which is the whole round trip. Split by method so uploads can be read apart from reads.
spec.title: TTFB
